_about: Hand-written for the demo (not model output). r = 1 only so the sample can be published; no person has reviewed it.

items.st: The warmth in the centre of the hive helps young bees to develop.
items.why: Line 1 says young bees need this warmth to grow.

items.st: Some bees cool the hive by moving air with their wings.
items.why: Lines 3 and 4 say workers fan their wings to push warm air out and pull cooler air in.

items.st: Water that dries on the walls of the hive helps to lower the temperature.
items.why: Line 6 says the drying water takes heat away.

items.st: The bees at the edge of the winter ball never change their position.
items.why: Line 9 says the bees on the outside slowly swap places with those in the middle.

items.st: The bees fan their wings at the back of the hive, far from the entrance.
items.why: Line 3 says the workers stand near the entrance when they fan.

items.st: In winter the bees make heat by fanning their wings near the entrance.
items.why: Line 8 says they make heat by shivering their flight muscles inside a ball.

items.st: A hive can hold more than fifty thousand bees in summer.
items.why: The passage never says how many bees live in a hive.

items.st: The queen stays in the middle of the ball because she is the largest bee.
items.why: Line 8 puts the ball around the queen but gives no reason for it.

items.st: Bees prefer to collect water from clean streams rather than from ponds.
items.why: Line 5 names ponds and streams but does not say which the bees prefer.
